full_judgment:
Moyeenul Islam Chowdhury J: A Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the judgment dated 29-12-1998 (Annexure-'A-4') passed by the Magistrate, 1st Class, Thakurgaon in GR Case No. 128 of 1991 corresponding to Thakurgaon Police Station Case No. 18 dated 31-8-1991 in so far as it relates to the petitioner No. 2 Md Abdul Latif, son of Joynal Mondal of Village-Shakdahchar, PS Mirpur, District-Kushtia convicting him under Section 408 of the Penal Code, 1960 and sentencing him the reunder to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 6(six) months in absentia should not be declared to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect and why a direction should not be given for further police investigation and submitting further police report for required correction of the trial Court's records of the said criminal case showing proper identity and particulars of the respondent No. 4 and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 5. At the outset, Mr Abdur Rezaque Khan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners, submits that it is on record that the petitioner No. 1 physically handed over the actual accused Md Abdul Latif (respondent No. 4) and the co-accused to the police at the time of lodgment of the FIR with the concerned Police Station and subsequently they were released on bail and at one state, they absconded and ultimately the impugned order of conviction and sentence was passed in absentia and as the petitioner No. 2 Md Abdul Latif, son of Md Joynal Mondal was mistakenly convicted and sentenced' instead of the respondent No. 4 Md Abdul Latif, son of Muzibar Rahman Biswas, the impugned order is not sustainable in law.
